reason: The idea's own timeline (scored Mon 28 ~08:00-10:00, about 24 h of slack) is achievable only if every link holds, and its pre-registered gate makes a scored probe unlikely. P(scored LB probe before 29 Sep 10:00) is about 0.1, far below 0.7. The links: (1) Lab data and compute. replay.py has no image access (deepcenter_bundle=None, replay.py l.881), so the DoG stage needs the raw TRAIN zarr. Only friend A (82 GB locally) or a Kaggle CPU kernel with the competition data attached has it. Friend A has made no commits since 24 Sep 04:12 MSK. His queued job is the x138 lab cache after #34 (PROMPT_FRIEND_A.md top block; 13-16 GPU-h per the sibling schedule verdicts), so the DoG grid competes with the team's higher-priority line. P(he runs the grid and the confirmation by Sun 27 ~12:00) ~0.5. The Kaggle CPU fallback runs through tools/kaggle_lab.py, which is PAUSED and unfinished (CONTEXT l.1546). It needs +3-5 h of agent work plus Vitalii's pushes, and adds only ~+0.05-0.1. (2) The 'required' honest-transfer step (12 LOEO-44b6 with the scratch detector) needs full-stack graphs on friend_a_exp02_loeo20. Only friend B (inactive) ever ran the full stack on that primary (RESULTS.md l.86-106). Friend A would have to re-run it (~1 h GPU+CPU) on the same GPU his x138 cache is using. Without friend A the protocol as written cannot be satisfied. (3) Gate. Idea P=0.4, sibling value verdict ~0.1: the reachable pool is ~90-150 FN, since runs of 6 or more hold only ~300 internal FN edges, and clearance kills the same-blob offsets. I use 0.2. By protocol a failed gate means no submission, so P(scored) ~0.55 x 0.2 x 0.85 (kernel + dummy + user OK + slot) ~0.09. Even ignoring the gate, ~0.55-0.6 x 0.85 ~0.5. (4) Implementation gaps. build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 supports ONLY divinsert|leafprune (docstring l.13-14), so dogrescue is a new patch anchored in x138 cell 5 (2.5-3 h, as stated). The runtime is not handled. DoG costs 0.14-0.18 s/frame here (my benchmark; confirms the idea's 0.15+0.11 s). Add ~0.05 s blosc read and ~1.5-2x slower Kaggle vCPU, and the hidden test's 10-13k frames cost 0.9-1.4 h SERIAL inside the repair loop. That loop is sorted-order and single-threaded (x138 cell 5 l.2071-2116), and the stage, like divinsert, sits outside the REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=27000 guard. Every DoG second therefore moves later movies toward the 7.5 h line, where relink/readmit/gapfill/safe divisions/linefit switch off (~-0.04 per degraded movie, h_kaggle-intel notes). The x138 hidden runtime is unknown (no logs; #34 latency tonight is the only proxy). A 4-video dummy run cannot reveal this (dummy times of 29-43 min are noise). (5) Lab base mismatch. The lab uses exp39 tails, but the submission uses x138, which has -2.9% nodes plus readmit (1,337 nodes on dummy) and gapfill (<=3%). Clearance vs final nodes, and the node-ratio gate, are measured on a different graph. No x138 lab exists; friend A's x138 cache would arrive Sun at the earliest (P~0.4-0.5). (6) A scored probe is uninformative anyway: the central public gain (+0.0005 value verdict; +0.001..+0.003 idea) sits inside the 0.003 LB noise. It spends 1 of 21 shared slots and ~1 GPU-h of dummy time that the x138 base / divins / finals lines need. Numbers checked: a_never 1,907 (6bba 1,740 / 44b6 167) matches fn_anatomy_exp39.md; the DoG CPU cost matches.

Latest safe submit: Mon 28 ~24:00 UTC for a score by 29 Sep ~10:00. A blind LB probe without the lab would be schedulable (kernel Sat, submit Sat/Sun, P(scored) ~0.8), but it skips the honest validation and could not tell +0.0005 from noise, so I do not recommend it.
